page.howto:
How to Use

Bible Green is a Bible app that lets you read the New Testament in Japanese, all the way to the nuance of the Greek original \u2014 no Greek required. There are just three things to do.

1. Tap a verse

Tap a verse in the chapter you are reading, and its words line up in the original order.

2. Tap a word

Tap a word to see its meaning and what it is doing in the sentence. To go deeper, \u201cLook up this word\u2019s meaning and usage\u201d opens the diagram of the sentence and the word\u2019s dictionary meanings.

3. Change how you read

You can change the reading mode from the menu\u2019s \u201cReading Mode\u201d.

Read in KougoStart by reading straight through in the familiar Japanese translation
Word OrderFollow the original order and check the Japanese, word by word
Sentence StructureReorder the sentence along its structure, then read

Reading the diagram

The diagram in the word analysis shows how the word you picked relates to the other words in the sentence. \u201cHow to read the marks\u201d, at the top of the diagram, explains the symbols.

To learn more

\u201cWorth Knowing\u201d has notes on how to read verbs, the article, and the cases.

Try it yourself

A guided tour walks you through famous passages in Romans and John\u2019s Gospel.
page.appinfo:
Design Philosophy

This app aims to bring the Greek text of the New Testament closer to the experience of reading. Rather than leaning on grammatical terminology, it shows the aspect of verbs \u2014 the quality of an action as it unfolds in time \u2014 with visual marks, so that the nuance of the original can be felt intuitively.

Solid line\u3000Present The action is still going on. It marks repetition, or something in progress.
Dotted line\u3000Aorist Something that happened as one event. Not a continuing past, but a point of fact.
Wavy line\u3000Perfect The result of something that happened still remains. Past and present stay connected.
Double line\u3000Future Something that will certainly happen \u2014 or the certainty and will to bring it about.
*\u3000Middle / Passive Shows whether the action extends to the subject itself (middle), or is received from outside (passive).
Background color\u3000Indicative / Imperative The verbs that carry the sentence: statements of fact, or strong calls to action.

About the Japanese in This App (Reading Japanese)

The Japanese shown in this app is not an ordinary \u201ctranslation\u201d. It is Japanese for reading the structure of the Greek text \u2014 number, gender, person, case, deixis, and more.

It reflects only what can be determined from the text itself, such as form and structure, and never fills gaps by guesswork or settles a word\u2019s meaning one-sidedly. The original text stays the starting point, in a form you can follow by reading.

The full thinking is published as the \u201cReading Japanese Specification\u201d.

Sources

Greek TextSBL Greek New Testament (SBLGNT)
\u00a9 Faithlife / Logos Bible Software, edited by Michael W. Holmes \u2014 CC BY 4.0
Morphological AnalysisMACULA Greek Linguistic Datasets, available at https://github.com/Clear-Bible/macula-greek/
\u00a9 Biblica, Inc. \u2014 CC BY 4.0
LexiconAbbott-Smith, A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
Syntactic Classification Wallace, Daniel B. Greek Grammar Beyond the Basics. Zondervan, 1996.
Wallace\u2019s grammatical classification and methods of analysis serve as a reference; the explanations themselves are written independently, for Japanese readers.
Japanese Translations The Kougo (Colloquial) Version (Japan Bible Society, 1955) and the Bungo (Literary) Version (Japan Bible Society, revised 1917)

Privacy

This app does not currently send or collect personal information or access logs on any server. Your reading progress and onboarding state are stored only in your browser\u2019s localStorage, and are never sent to a server.

If a future feature ever requires collecting information, that change will be announced in advance and made only with your consent.

On the Use of AI

No AI is used in any of the core reading functions of this app: displaying the biblical text, morphological analysis, syntactic information, or dictionary lookup.

The Greek text, Japanese text, word-form information, grammatical information, and dictionary and search data shown in the app are all based on scholarly data sources.

AI is used only as coding support during development, and as an aid in translating and preparing dictionary data.

The biblical text and grammatical information provided in this app are therefore not generated by AI.
